sessions.goal: Play as a brand-new player who has never heard of the game, following the HUD's NEXT line (top left) from the first afternoon until you have slept at home and woken the next morning; then try V. Note every moment of confusion, and answer the questions at the end.
sessions.verdict: The core sequence (pots that are clay, a coiled snake that becomes rope under a steady lamp, a codex page with Sanskrit and translation unlocking at each beat) is clear, quiet and lands well, and the NEXT line with distance hints carried me through without getting lost. The two long waits are the weak spots: the sunset wait and especially the dream after sleeping have no feedback and no hint, and the dream's backwards-running clock felt like a hang. secondsToObjective are wall-clock seconds from pt start (no probe), inflated by a slow shared software renderer.
questions: In your own words, what did you think the game was about? What did the rope and the snake, and the clay and the pots, mean?
Did anything feel preachy, confusing, or inaccurate (in the teaching, the verses in the codex, or how the tradition is described)? Say what and where; if nothing did, say so.

answers.question: In your own words, what did you think the game was about? What did the rope and the snake, and the clay and the pots, mean?
answers.answer: An ordinary village day used to show that what we take as many separate things are names and shapes laid over one reality. The pots I made and named (Ganga, Moon, Sparrow) were, seen through the clay lens, just clay; breaking one changed nothing real, like space in a pot rejoining space. The snake on the dusk path was fear projected onto something not seen clearly; looking steadily with the lamp showed it was only ever a rope, and the fear meter dropped. Together they seemed to say the world of many things is like that snake: a mistaken appearance over the one Self, which clear seeing removes. The dream and waking, and 'Nothing more is asked of you' with V to step back and watch, felt like the waking state seen as another dream and the self as witness.

answers.question: Did anything feel preachy, confusing, or inaccurate (in the teaching, the verses in the codex, or how the tradition is described)? Say what and where; if nothing did, say so.
answers.answer: Nothing felt preachy: the codex only appears when you ask for it, cites sources (Chandogya Upanisad 6.1.4, Gaudapada Mandukya Karika 2.17-18 and 3.3-4) with Sanskrit, transliteration and translation, and the italic notes are short. The rope-and-snake note's line that the village, chores and people are 'that kind of error; they are real for living in' was a careful touch. I cannot judge accuracy of the Sanskrit or translations. Confusing: the dream after sleeping ('Nothing here seems strange', clock running backwards) - I could not tell what it was teaching or whether I was meant to do something; the one line of meaning I guessed (dream vs waking) was never stated. I did not open the 'Other schools' page, so cannot say how other traditions are described.

sessions.goal: Clay and pots: at the potter's wheel throw three pots (1-4) and name each one, use the clay lens (C) and look around with it, break a pot (B), then read what opened in the codex (Tab). Then carry on toward dusk as far as your time allows, and answer the questions at the end.
sessions.verdict: The clay-and-pots loop works end to end: throwing three pots, naming them, then seeing 'Ganga: clay' under the lens and breaking one to open Gaudapada's pot-space verse lands its idea quietly. The rope reveal at dusk, with Fear filling and then draining under the lamp, is the strongest moment I played. What mostly gets in the way is how the screen reads: the wheel looks like a shadow, finished pots appear out of view, and several text overlaps and cut-off lines show at 640x360. The sunset wait is long and gives no feedback. secondsToObjective is wall-clock seconds from pt start; the game has no probe.

answers.question: Did anything feel preachy, confusing, or inaccurate (in the teaching, the verses in the codex, or how the tradition is described)? Say what and where; if nothing did, say so.
answers.answer: Nothing felt preachy. The game shows rather than lectures, and the 'Other schools' codex page fairly gives the Vishishtadvaita (Ramanuja) and Dvaita (Madhva) readings of 'tat tvam asi' and says the game follows one school. Small confusions: that page mentions the snake and rope before I had met them at dusk, which is a mild spoiler. The pot-space and rope-snake pages say their translations are a 'working translation ... awaiting review', so I could not judge their accuracy. I am not qualified to judge the Sanskrit; nothing looked wrong to me.

sessions.goal: The rope: do what the NEXT line asks until dusk, then walk the path from the village to the ghat, light the lamp (F) and look steadily at each snake until it turns out to be a rope; then sleep at home (E at the indigo door) and, in the morning, try V. Answer the questions at the end.
sessions.verdict: The pots-into-clay and snake-into-rope beats both work and land well: the clay lens relabelling every named pot as 'clay', and a coiled snake turning into an orange rope after about 3 s of steady lamplight, are clear, quiet payoffs, and the codex pages give sources and fair readings from several schools. What went wrong was sleeping: 'sleep until morning' led to a dream with the clock running backward and the NEXT line 'Nothing here seems strange', no way forward and no morning, so V in the morning could not be tested (V in the dream says stepping out comes later). The other issues are the unmeasured sunset wait and several HUD lines that clip or wash out at 640x360. secondsToObjective is wall-clock time (no probe), slowed by about 5 fps headless.

sessions.goal: As a brand-new player, follow the NEXT line from the first afternoon (the potter's wheel, then dusk and the snakes on the path) until you sleep at home after both teachings. Describe exactly what happens after you sleep (the dream, the deep sleep), whether anything made you think the game had stopped or frozen, then read the codex pages that open when you wake and try V and the after-mode chores. Answer the questions at the end.
sessions.verdict: The NEXT line carried me cleanly from the wheel through the snakes to sleep, and the snake-into-rope under the lamp and the waking codex pages are the high points. The dream gives no cue for over a minute and the deep sleep is an unlabelled black screen, so both look like the game has hung; one quiet caption each would fix that. secondsToObjective are wall-clock seconds on a heavily loaded stepped headless run (about 8x slower than real time), not game time.

findings.title: Dream after sleeping gives no instruction and cannot be shortened; clock runs backwards for ~100 game seconds
findings.detail: After E at the door ('You sleep, and dream.') the world turns grey, the HUD clock runs backwards (6:56 pm -> 6:03 -> 4:33 -> 2:46 -> 11:43 am) and NEXT says only 'Nothing here seems strange'. Walking, E, C, F1 help and the codex give no hint of what to do or how to wake. It ended on its own at 22 March 7:07 am after roughly 100 game seconds (about 13 minutes wall-clock on this machine). A new player would likely think the game had hung or that they were meant to find something. Expected: a NEXT line such as 'Wait for morning' or a shorter dream.
findings.repro: pt start --profile atman-strata --game-dir /root/atman-proctor-030 --seed 1; follow NEXT through pots, ghat, three ropes; E at your door; pt wait 15 repeatedly and pt shot
alsoTitled: Dream phase gives no instruction or end cue; clock runs backward for ~70 game-seconds
Sleeping at the indigo door starts a dream with a backward-running clock and no way forward shown; morning never came

findings.title: Deep sleep is a fully black screen with no HUD or caption: reads as a crash/freeze
findings.detail: At the end of the dream the screen goes completely black apart from one faint grey dot in the centre; HUD, clock and captions all disappear. Nothing tells the player this is deep sleep or that the game is still running. It lasted under ~10 game-seconds here and then I woke on 22 March 6:39 am, but a player at that moment has no way to know it will end. Expected: a quiet caption ('Deep sleep. Nothing appears.') or a slowly breathing light so the player knows it is intended.
findings.repro: pt start --profile atman-strata --game-dir /root/atman-proctor-030 --seed 4; complete wheel, break a pot, wait for sunset at the ghat, turn 3 snakes to rope, E at your door; pt wait ~85 in total; shot shows black screen

findings.title: NEXT line during the rope/snake step is cut off at the right edge, hiding the (n of 3) counter
findings.detail: After the first snake becomes a rope the NEXT line reads 'Go closer with the lamp, then look at it steadily (1' and is clipped at the window edge in 640x360; the 'Hold the lamp to it ... (2 of 3' line is also clipped. The counter is the only clue that there are three.
findings.repro: on the dusk path, light the lamp (F), look steadily at the first coil until it turns to rope; pt shot
alsoTitled: NEXT line cut off at the right edge after the first rope ('...look at it steadily (1')
NEXT snake counter runs off the right edge at 640x360
Text runs off the 640x360 window: NEXT snake counter and after-mode caption

findings.title: Opening intro message overlaps the help block on the first screen
findings.detail: On start the orange line 'The NEXT line, top left, says what comes next.' is drawn over the help's first line 'W A S D walk ... E use', making both unreadable until F1 hides the help.
alsoTitled: Opening help overlaps the orange intro hint
Opening hint overlaps the help panel's first line at game start

findings.title: Waiting on the ghat steps for the sunset gives no feedback for ~55 in-game minutes
findings.detail: Standing on the steps from 5:27 to about 6:21 pm, NEXT stays 'Wait on the ghat steps for the sunset' with no countdown, no 'you sit and watch' message, and E does nothing. A player cannot tell whether they are in the right place. When it ended, NEXT switched straight to 'Light your lamp (F)' with no sunset moment acknowledged.
findings.repro: after breaking a pot, walk to the ghat steps until the distance hint disappears; pt wait 8; pt key e; pt wait 25; pt shot
alsoTitled: E at the ghat gives no feedback; the sunset wait gives no sense of how long
Waiting on the ghat steps for the sunset gives no sense of how long the wait is

findings.title: Thrown pots do not appear at the wheel; they land on a bench behind the player
findings.detail: After throwing and naming three pots at the wheel nothing is visible on or by the wheel. Only the next step's distance hint ('4 m behind you, to the right') reveals they are on a drying board behind. Breaking one also needs very precise aim ('Look straight at one of your pots, close by') and the clay lens view is so dark the pots are hard to find.
findings.repro: at the wheel: pt key 1; pt wait 6; pt type Ganga; pt key Return; repeat with 2 and 3; pt shot
alsoTitled: Thrown pots appear behind the player, out of view, with no feedback at the wheel

findings.title: After-mode chores have no direction hint and E at the well does nothing
findings.detail: After waking, NEXT reads 'Nothing more is asked of you' and the chores stay listed '(as you like)', but they no longer show a distance/direction and I could not find what E does at the well. A new player has no lead to start the chores. (I ran out of time before walking to the ghat or clay bank.)
findings.repro: after waking: walk to the well, pt key e

findings.title: Lamp-lit wall up close washes out the HUD; door distance points through the house
findings.detail: Going home at night with the lamp lit, a house wall close in front turns pale yellow and the white HUD text over it (NEXT/CHORES/MADE) is nearly unreadable. Also, 'Go home and sleep (E at your door) 6 m ahead' pointed straight through my house wall, because the door is on the far side, facing the well. I walked into the wall: one frame was solid dark grey, then I had to back off and go around.
findings.repro: after the third rope: hurry toward the house following NEXT; pt shot x when against the wall

findings.title: Opening tutorial line is overlapped by the help overlay
findings.detail: On start, the orange line 'The NEXT line, top left, says what comes next' is drawn underneath the white help rows (WASD walk / F lamp ...), so both are partly unreadable until F1 hides the help.

findings.title: Potter's wheel is an unreadable dark disc on the ground; NEXT says '3 m ahead' while standing beside it
findings.detail: Following NEXT ('Throw pots at the potter's wheel ... 3 m ahead') I stopped next to a dark flat disc I took for a shadow. Pressing 1 did nothing and no prompt appeared until I looked down and walked onto the disc. Expected a recognisable wheel (rim, stool, spinning head) and the 'At the wheel' prompt within ~2 m.
findings.repro: pt start --profile atman-strata --seed 2; F1; look left ~-670 px total; walk with Shift+W ~10 s toward the wheel until NEXT reads '3 m ahead'; press 1 (nothing); look 0 150; hold w 1.5 -> wheel prompt appears

findings.title: Wheel prompt is drawn over the HUD CHORES/MADE lists when the HUD is shown
findings.detail: With the HUD visible at the wheel, 'At the wheel: 1 water jar 2 bowl 3 cup 4 lamp' is centered over the chore lines and wraps '4 lamp' onto the MADE header row. The naming prompt also sits on the CHORES lines.
findings.repro: Stand on the wheel with the HUD on (H); pt shot

findings.title: Codex page titles truncated in the left list
findings.detail: 'The space in the pot' and 'The rope and the snake' are cut off ('The space in the pot', 'The rope and the sna') by the left column width.
alsoTitled: Codex list entry 'The space in the pot' clipped by page panel

findings.title: Codex body text is very small at 640x360
findings.detail: Codex pages have Devanagari, IAST, translation and commentary in small serif type; at 640x360 the commentary and source lines are about 6 px tall and hard to read. The pages themselves are excellent.

findings.title: HUD text unreadable against lamp-lit walls
findings.detail: White HUD text has no backing panel or outline; beside a house wall lit by the lamp the NEXT and CHORES lines nearly vanish into bright yellow.
findings.repro: walk home at dusk with the lamp lit and face your house wall; pt shot

findings.title: Opening hint 'Your house is beside you' stays on screen after walking away
findings.detail: The hint 'Your house is beside you; its door, the indigo one, faces the well' stayed up after I had walked 20 m away to the wheel, where it was no longer true.
findings.repro: pt key F1; walk toward the wheel; pt shot x

findings.title: Pot targeting for B is fiddly and HUD covers the wheel area
findings.detail: The MADE list and chores block cover the lower left where the pots sit, and the crosshair must be exactly on a pot before 'B break the Moon' shows; it took 4 look adjustments. Thrown pots also never appeared in view while throwing; I only saw them after turning around.
findings.repro: throw 3 pots at the wheel, press C, then try B

findings.title: Text clipped or badly wrapped in several places
findings.detail: The codex page list clips long titles at the panel edge ('The space in the pot' and 'The rope and the sna...'). The wheel prompt '1 water jar 2 bowl 3 cup 4 lamp' wraps so that 'lamp' sits alone on the next line, apart from its '4'. 'Look straight at one of your pots, close by, to break it (B).' first appeared cut off at the bottom of the screen. The 'Other schools' codex page is very small, dense serif text at 640x360.
findings.repro: pt key Tab after the first codex page appears; stand at the wheel

findings.title: V (step back and watch) first puts the camera inside a house wall
findings.detail: On waking beside a house, V initially showed half the screen as a flat grey slab; after about 3 seconds the camera settled behind the figure walking on its own, which is a lovely moment.
findings.repro: after waking, pt key v; pt step 30; pt shot
